keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the republic's real life, 16 October 1796 to 29 June 1797, which Cliopatria lacks. The congress of 16 October 1796 was 'formed by representatives from the provinces of Modena, Bologna, Ferrara and Reggio Emilia'. The page gives no area; the four modern provinces are about 10,000 km2 on the grid.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, but not the Cispadane Republic: for 1800..1802 it is Modena-Reggio land inside the restored Cisalpine Republic. The Cispadane Republic ended on 29 June 1797

keyframe_review.note: 7,095 km2 for 1800..1802, 31 cells: Modena 10, Reggio Emilia 8, Parma 4, Mantova 3, Ferrara 2 and one cell each in Rovigo, Massa-Carrara, Lucca and Bologna. The page says 'On 29 June 1797, the Cispadane Republic united with the Transpadane Republic to form the Cisalpine Republic' and says nothing about 1800-1802. The cisalpine-republic dossier keyframes 1800..1802 for the whole restored Cisalpine Republic, which holds this land.

ledger.note: 16 October 1796: the congress of Modena creates the Cispadane Republic. 'On 16 October 1796, a congress was held in Modena' after the duke fled, 'formed by representatives from the provinces of Modena, Bologna, Ferrara and Reggio Emilia'; the session of 7 January 1797 at Reggio Emilia decided to form a government. Capital Bologna.

wars.outcome: Napoleon's army took Modena and the Papal Legations from their rulers; they became the Cispadane Republic and then, on 29 June 1797, part of the Cisalpine Republic. The page's infobox dates: Battle of Lodi 10 May 1796, Treaty of Tolentino 19 February 1797, Treaty of Campo Formio 17 October 1797.
wars.note: Named from the page's infobox events; the page does not narrate the campaign, and no campaign date inside the four provinces is on it.

certainty.note: The republic is four provinces named at a congress; the page gives no boundary and its territory was settled only as French armies took it.

sources.title: Cispadane Republic
sources.note: Infobox (dates, capital, predecessors), the congress of 16 October 1796, the four provinces, the union of 29 June 1797; nothing on 1800-1802.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Cispadane Republic' row (1800..1802, one shape of 7,095 km2) does not describe this state: the republic existed from the congress of 16 October 1796 to the union with the Transpadane Republic on 29 June 1797, and the page says nothing about 1800-1802. The 31 cells are Modena-Reggio land that the restored Cisalpine Republic held in those years (see the cisalpine-republic dossier, which keyframes 1800..1802). The row is marked wrong and a keyframe for 1796..1797 is added; the Cliopatria years are not this state's. Not settled: the page lists the Duchy of Massa and Carrara as a predecessor without detail (no territory event); the date of the Legations' secession from the Papal States (the page gives only the congress date); the Reggio congress of 27 December 1796 is not on the page; the Cisalpine page used by the cisalpine-republic dossier gives 27 July 1797 for the merger, this page 29 June 1797. Counterparts needing dossiers: duchy-of-massa-and-carrara, transpadane-republic (named by the Cisalpine note). Page budget: 1 of 1-2 pages.
